question: Should model-originated opaque `channelData` be recursively inspected and dropped as a whole whenever any key or value contains protected internal runtime context?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but this choice defines a cross-provider security and message-delivery contract for opaque payloads; code inspection cannot decide the acceptable false-positive tradeoff on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Confirm fail-closed suppression
options.body: Keep the recursive scan and whole-payload deletion, document the invariant in code/tests, then rebase and validate the exact head.

options.title: Narrow the security policy
options.body: Limit filtering to an explicitly defined safe schema or owner-provided contract before allowing stringified channel data to become dispatchable.

options.title: Pause opaque payload support
options.body: Do not merge stringified channelData dispatch until a typed or channel-owned validation boundary is designed.

recommendation.title: Confirm fail-closed suppression
recommendation.body: Keep the recursive scan and whole-payload deletion, document the invariant in code/tests, then rebase and validate the exact head.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans both the Agents message-tool path and an outbound security boundary, matching the listed Agents and Security ownership areas.
